title: Making Large Organizations Feel Smaller
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses a common growth pain: as organizations scale, they tend to lose the camaraderie and personal connection typical of small teams. The author offers several concrete practices leaders can use to counter this — frequent, personally-directed (not mass-blast) communication from senior leadership, genuine open Q&A forums with real follow-through, breaking large groups into smaller weekly pods for substantive discussion, and visible leader presence. The piece emphasizes that size alone doesn't determine organizational feel; deliberate leadership choices can preserve intimacy and community regardless of headcount.
points: Frequent, personally-directed communication from senior leaders (especially the CEO) recreates the intimacy of a smaller organization even as headcount grows.
Open forums with genuine Q&A, and following up on what people suggested, build trust that a large organization is still listening to individuals.
Breaking large organizations into small pods that meet weekly for real conversation (not status updates) preserves a sense of community.
Making an organization feel smaller reduces anonymity and increases commitment, regardless of actual headcount.
quotes: As organizations and teams grow and add more people, it is easy to lose the camaraderie and personal connection between team members.
The more messages that are personally directed, as opposed to group chain communications, the more they recreate the conversations team members experience in smaller enterprises.
When team members get to ask the questions that matter to them and receive genuine and candid answers, they feel more connected to the organization and to each other.
Be sure to circle back and close the loop on what people suggested, even if it runs contrary to the eventual outcome.
When organizations feel smaller, they foster more connection, reduce anonymity, and create a strong sense of community.
